title: Hybrid offline-online machine learning framework for real-time UAV battery voltage prediction
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAV) are destined to become a reliable, customizable and versatile assets in all those logistic applications where precision, speed, and high mission readability are required. However, one of the reasons which is hindering its seamless adoption is the lack of a consolidated body of literature on energy and voltage prediction strategies. In the scarce panorama of Machine Learning (ML) energy and voltage online prediction methodologies for UAVs, this paper proposes a highly scalable strategy to address the ongoing challenges associated with UAV battery monitoring. The methodology presents a novel offline flight multi-criteria segmentation strategy combined with a customizable online discrepancy-triggered update based on Continuous Ranked Probability Score (CRPS) metric. Moreover, multi-physics battery modeling, together with a Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) trained on as many as 200 drone flights, is used to model battery behavior and to provide the user with the battery voltage trend before cut-off. The framework has been evaluated using a publicly accessible dataset, demonstrating its effectiveness in predicting voltage trends for future planned flights and its ability to improve prediction accuracy during flight operations. The overall work incorporates innovative methodologies with a focus on practical applicability, thus facilitating the advancement of ML strategies in these domains.

title: Telemetry-driven physics-informed prediction for on-orbit thermal–electrical performance of solar panels in satellite power system
abstract: For small satellites and CubeSat missions, body-mounted solar panels serve as the primary and often sole source of onboard power. Accurate prediction of the on-orbit thermal–electrical performance of small satellite solar panels is critical for power system management and health monitoring. However, it remains challenging due to complex orbital environments, unstable attitude motion, and limited availability of high-fidelity telemetry information. This paper proposes a physics-informed machine learning (PIML) prediction model for satellite solar panels under uncertain orbital environment conditions. The proposed approach avoids reliance on detailed flight information by converting measured telemetry into physically admissible information. A telemetry-driven orbital environment inversion strategy is developed to infer the solar panel’s thermal environment from real-time telemetry data. Based on the equivalent environmental states, a thermal–electrical soft constraint model is constructed to define a limiting scope of operation. The resulting physics-informed constraints are fused with telemetry data and used as hybrid inputs to PIML prediction models, encoded by recurrent neural networks (RNN) and long short-term memory networks (LSTM). The prediction model is evaluated using real-time telemetry from the TURUS satellite. Multiple prediction scenarios are designed, and the results demonstrate that the PIML prediction model is stable, physical consistent, and generalized. This study provides a practical solution for on-orbit thermal–electrical performance prediction under telemetry-limited conditions.

title: Conditional physics-informed deep operator networks for low earth orbit satellite trajectory prediction
abstract: With the deployment of large-scale constellations, accurate orbit prediction for Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites is critical for space situational awareness. The increasing complexity of these mega-constellations also imposes significant challenges on dynamic topology management [1] and inter-satellite routing [2], where precise orbital information serves as a fundamental prerequisite. The standard SGP4 model has limited accuracy, while purely data-driven methods often lack physical consistency and generalization capabilities. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a prediction framework based on a Conditional Physics-Informed Deep Operator Network (Conditional PI-DeepONet). The model utilizes the DeepONet architecture to learn a general operator that maps a satellite’s initial conditions to its full state trajectory, enabling flexible predictions from any given epoch. By incorporating the governing orbital dynamics-including central gravity, J2 perturbation, and atmospheric drag-as a soft constraint in the loss function, the framework ensures the physical self-consistency of the predictions. Furthermore, a system reduction technique is employed to enhance training stability. Based on a high-quality dataset with ground truth labels from the International Laser Ranging Service (ILRS), we conduct comprehensive experiments in both single-satellite and multi-satellite scenarios. The results demonstrate that the proposed PINN model significantly outperforms SGP4 and a data-only baseline model in terms of prediction accuracy. This study validates the effectiveness of the proposed framework as a high-precision, flexible tool for LEO orbit prediction.

title: A physics-informed sparse coding framework for reconstruction of multiple impulsive maneuvers
abstract: Characterizing the motion of non-cooperative space objects is essential for space situational awareness, yet traditional orbit determination often fails when unknown maneuvers occur. Precisely maintaining orbital custody and ensuring collision safety require accurate, efficient reconstruction of these impulsive maneuvers. However, existing methods struggle to simultaneously reconstruct the timing, magnitude, and direction of multiple impulsive maneuvers with low computational effort. This paper proposes a physics-informed sparse coding framework that integrates physical dynamics and sparse coding techniques to reconstruct multiple unknown impulsive maneuvers from tracking data. This method models thrust as a temporally group-sparse exogenous input and integrates high-fidelity dynamics with measurements in an efficient batch projected formulation, which significantly reduces the computational burden while maintaining reconstruction accuracy. A projection step analytically eliminates the initial-state uncertainty, yielding a reduced thrust-only convex problem. The maneuver reconstructions can be obtained from solving this problem through group-sparsity-aware optimization techniques. Numerical simulations indicate that the proposed method accurately reconstructs multiple impulsive maneuvers in high-fidelity scenarios, including low Earth, medium Earth, highly elliptical orbits, and several real-world cases. These results demonstrate the adaptability of the proposed framework to realistic operating conditions, positioning the framework as a powerful tool for maneuver inference and intent characterization in realistic operational scenarios.

title: A detailed geometry-free approach for propeller performance prediction using machine learning models
abstract: • Framework that predicts unseen 2-bladed propellers performance at varying conditions. • Mixed dataset improves robustness and aligns predictions with experiments. • MLP model outperforms BEMT predictions across wide operating conditions. Accurate and fast prediction of aerodynamic forces is an essential step in the design of any Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV), in particular the prediction of the thrust and torque produced by a propeller. Existing approaches to this span from low-fidelity Blade Element Momentum Theory (BEMT) to high fidelity Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) or even experimental testing and present different trade-offs between accuracy, cost, and practicality. This work introduces a machine learning approach to predict thrust and torque for 2-bladed propellers by APC manufacturer with diameters between 7 and 20 inches. To train the Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) used in this approach, a mixed dataset was built by combining numerical data generated through an adapted BEMT implementation with experimental data gathered from wind tunnel tests on 19 propellers. The results show that the model accurately predicts thrust and torque under various operational conditions, reaching values below 10% for thrust and demonstrating reliability comparable to traditional methods while significantly reducing computational or experimental demands. This study confirms the viability of machine learning as a predictive tool for propeller performance of small UAV, especially in early-stages of the design process where fast, reliable estimates are needed.

title: Data-efficient neural operator surrogates for nonlinear pitch dynamics of blunt-body re-entry vehicles
abstract: Accurate prediction of blunt body pitch dynamics during atmospheric entry is challenged by nonlinear aerodynamics, experimental limitations, and the prohibitive cost of free-flight CFD (FF-CFD). Previous FF-CFD-based system identification and Bayesian inference approaches using Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) are computationally intensive, data-hungry, and sensitive to prior knowledge. To address these limitations, a neural ordinary differential equation (neural ODE) surrogate is developed to learn continuous-time pitching dynamics directly from trajectory data. The study is carried out in two phases at Mach 1.44 using simulated free-flight data of ballistic-range experiments of the Genesis sample return capsule. The first phase consists of a synthetic study, where controlled trajectory data are used to evaluate the extrapolation and generalization behavior. Training on a single initial condition with short time windows of 0.7s extrapolated accurately to 1.4s, whereas training on multiple initial conditions at angles-of-attack of 1∘ and 20∘ generalized across the 1∘-40∘ range. The reconstructed dynamic stability coefficient agrees with MCMC benchmarks, demonstrating accurate recovery of nonlinear stability behavior. In the second phase, FF-CFD simulations were conducted using initial angles-of-attack 1∘ and 20∘ for training and 2∘, 5∘, 10∘, and 30∘ for validation. The neural ODE reproduces oscillatory responses with an approximately 1∘ error, generalizes to both the in- and out-of-distribution regimes, and provides calibrated uncertainty bands with variational inference. Compared to MCMC-based inverse estimation, the proposed neural ODE approach achieves higher predictive accuracy. These results demonstrate that neural ODE surrogates offer a data-efficient, uncertainty-aware, and scalable framework for re-entry vehicle stability analysis.

title: Goal-driven adaptive sampling strategies for machine learning models predicting fields
abstract: Machine learning models are widely regarded as a way forward to tackle multi-query challenges that arise once expensive black-box simulations such as computational fluid dynamics are investigated. However, ensuring the desired level of accuracy for a certain task at minimal computational cost, e.g. as few black-box samples as possible, remains a challenge. Active learning strategies are used for scalar quantities to overcome this challenge and different so-called infill criteria exist and are commonly employed in several scenarios. Even though needed in various fields, an extension of active learning strategies towards field predictions is still lacking or limited to very specific scenarios and/or model types. In this paper we propose an active learning strategy for machine learning models that are capable of predicting fields, which is agnostic to the model architecture itself. For doing so, we combine a well-established Gaussian process model for a scalar reference value and simultaneously aim at reducing the epistemic model error and the difference between scalar and field predictions. Different specific forms of the above-mentioned approach are introduced and compared to each other as well as only scalar-valued based infill. Results are presented for the NASA common research model for an uncertainty propagation task showcasing high level of accuracy at significantly smaller cost compared to an approach without active learning.

title: Hybrid Aero-PINN: A physics-consistent deep learning framework for efficient aerodynamic prediction
abstract:
Aerodynamic prediction across various operating conditions is a major challenge for data-driven models. They often struggle with limited generalisation, poor physical consistency, and excessive reliance on large datasets. This work introduces a Hybrid Aero-Physics-Informed Neural Network (Hybrid Aero-PINN) that integrates machine learning with aerodynamic theory to address these issues. The term physics-informed is used here in a structured, neuro-symbolic sense, where physical consistency is enforced through deterministic analytical operators rather than soft constraint enforcement of governing equations. Instead of treating finite-wing aerodynamics as a black-box problem, our framework decomposes the physics into two regimes. A deep neural network is trained to predict two-dimensional viscous airfoil coefficients from angle of attack, Reynolds number, camber, and thickness. This captures nonlinear boundary-layer and separation effects. The network's outputs then pass through a physics layer that analytically integrates the results to calculate three-dimensional lift, drag, and the lift-to-drag ratio using established aerodynamic principles. The author generates a high-quality dataset using XFOIL in a controlled pre-stall regime. The author rigorously filters this dataset using linearity, Reynolds scaling, and aspect ratio constraints to remove physically unstable samples. For benchmarking, a purely data-driven black-box neural network trained on the same dataset produces RMSE(L/D) = 0.966 and R² = 0.972 (L/D MAPE = 2.43%). The Hybrid Aero-PINN attains R²(L/D) = 0.9818 and L/D MAPE = 1.84% (sectional: R²(

title: A multi-stage AI-driven aerodynamic inverse design framework for 3D configurations: Application to high-bypass-ratio turbofan nacelles
abstract: The drag design of nacelles is significant for turbofan aero-engines with high-bypass-ratio. However, for the inverse design problem of complex three-dimensional(3D) configurations, the Pareto front solution of the multi-objective inverse design of 3D nacelle makes target distribution determination more complex and difficult. Additionally, existing experience is generally insufficient to complete the acquisition of target distributions. In this paper, a multi-stage AI-driven aerodynamic inverse design framework for 3D configurations is proposed. The proposed method incorporates dimensionality reduction of complex space, design feature analysis and extraction, optimization of target distribution, and aerodynamic inverse design to significantly im-prove the design efficiency. The multi-stage AI-driven aerodynamic inverse design framework can generate target distributions that satisfy the 3D effects, and flexibly adjust the target distributions during the process of optimization seeking. For saving the energy consumption of aero-engine, the multi-objective optimization of 3D nacelle is conducted with the drag coefficient and drag divergence performance as design targets. The flow mechanism and design law are revealed by analyzing the geometric distribution and the surface Isen-tropic Mach number distribution. This paper demonstrates the feasibility of the proposed multi-stage AI-driven aerodynamic inverse design method in the application of 3D nacelle design.

title: Robust high-fidelity dataset-based shape optimization for aircraft design
abstract: This paper demonstrates the feasibility of high-fidelity aerodynamic dataset-based aircraft shape optimization for mission performance improvements within an automated framework.The framework was applied to a simple, yet realistic test case: the Optimization Test Interceptor with Fan (OTIFAN) - a fixed-wing unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) featuring an internal electric ducted fan (EDF) propulsion system. To ensure viable aircraft designs, lower-fidelity methods are incorporated for the disciplines of mass properties, flight mechanics, and structural analysis. Three optimization strategies have been implemented and assessed: Grid search (GS) for setup and validation, gradient-based optimization (GO) for efficient local optimization and Bayesian optimization (BO) for global, gradient-free optimization. The strategies are applied across two objective functions, illustrating the applicability of the method to geometric, mission-profile and structural optimizations. This novel approach advances the state of the art in high-fidelity optimization for aircraft design and showcases the engineering potential for enhancing mission-based performance of industrially relevant configurations through automated optimization. While the application of high-fidelity RANS computations mitigates the limitations of simplified aerodynamics, robustness of the design is ensured by the aerodynamic dataset-based approach, in which the complete flight envelope is considered for each generated shape.

title: Physics-informed transformer with residual analysis and adaptive threshold Kalman filter for angle-of-attack sensor fault detection
abstract: The angle-of-attack (AoA) sensor is essential to modern aircraft systems; however, its vulnerability to faults has contributed to several aviation accidents. This study proposes two novel sensor fusion-based fault detection methods that combine data-driven techniques with physics principles: the Physics-Informed Transformer with Residual Analysis (PITRA) and the Adaptive Threshold Kalman Filter (ATKF). PITRA uses a physics-informed encoder-decoder transformer to construct a virtual AoA sensor. By incorporating reduced-order aircraft dynamics into the loss function and applying an adaptive weight (γadaptive) to balance physics-informed and data-driven losses, PITRA enhances AoA estimation. The ATKF augments a reduced-order aircraft model with sensor bias and gain parameters for fault detection using adaptive thresholding and Kalman filtering. Both methods are evaluated using using flight data from the Advanced Technologies Testing Aircraft System (ATTAS) under fault-free, faulty, and noisy sensor conditions. Sensitivity analyses with Gaussian and non-Gaussian sensor noise showed that PITRA (γadaptive) is more robust in noisy environments. During elevator maneuver with a 10% Gaussian noise-to-signal power ratio (NSPR) AoA sensor, PITRA achieved an average false positive rate (FPR) of 0, compared to 12.8 ± 19.8 for ATKF. PITRA (γadaptive, Noisy), trained on 70% of the dataset with 10% NSPR Gaussian noise, performed better with only minimal degradation. However, ATKF outperformed PITRA in terms of detection delay, identifying ramp faults in 0.18 seconds, compared to 0.44 seconds. The research shows that while physics-informed machine learning models require significant computational resources, they excel in noisy environments. In contrast, physics-based fault detection methods using Kalman filters are less resource-intensive and more effective.

title: PHD-NO: A physics-guided hash-encoding dual-branch neural operator for transonic supercritical airfoil aerodynamics
abstract:
Supercritical airfoils operating in transonic flows present an inherent multiscale challenge, where sharp shock discontinuities are coupled with delicate, attached boundary layer structures. Conventional neural operators often suffer from inherent spectral bias, where global smooth features are prioritized over high-frequency singularities or encounter non-physical Gibbs oscillations when attempting to resolve shocks via global encodings. To address this limitation, we propose the physics-guided hash-encoding dual-branch neural operator (PHD-NO). Its central design is a dual-branch hash-encoding architecture tailored to transonic aerodynamic fields, where the background flow and shock-dominated corrections are handled in a scale-decoupled manner. By employing multi-resolution hash grid encoding as a unified feature basis, the framework leverages the locally compact support of fine-resolution grids to achieve exceptional spatial precision at shock locations while maintaining global consistency through coarse-resolution levels. Theoretically, we analyze PHD-NO through the Neural Tangent Kernel framework and argue that the multi-scale hash sub-kernels can compensate for high-frequency eigenvalue decay over a broader frequency range, thereby mitigating the spectral-bias gap. On a high-fidelity supercritical-airfoil dataset, PHD-NO attains mean L1 errors at the 
10
−
3
 level, preserves accurate shock localization and surface-pressure reconstruction, and delivers up to about 474 ×  faster CPU-side inference than the CFD solver on the same hardware basis.

title: Deep deterministic policy gradient with symmetric data augmentation for lateral attitude tracking control of a fixed-wing aircraft
abstract: The symmetry of dynamical systems can be exploited for state-transition prediction and to facilitate control policy optimization. This paper leverages system symmetry to develop sample-efficient offline reinforcement learning (RL) approaches. Under the symmetry assumption for a Markov Decision Process (MDP), a symmetric data augmentation method is proposed. The augmented samples are integrated into the dataset of Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) to enhance its coverage of the state space. Furthermore, sample utilization efficiency is improved by introducing a second critic trained on the augmented samples, resulting in a dual-critic structure. The aircraft’s model is verified to be symmetric, and flight control simulations demonstrate accelerated policy convergence when augmented samples are employed.

title: Simulating and analyzing the flow field of an oscillating airfoil via physics-informed neural networks with data assimilation
abstract: Research on unsteady flow field of oscillating airfoil is closely related to the methods of handling turbulence problems. Experimental measurements and numerical simulations, both of which have their own limitations-high cost or inability to simultaneously achieve computational accuracy and efficiency. In this work, we proposed a physics-informed neural network model based on data assimilation (DA-PINN) to simulate and analyze the flow field of the National Advisory Committee for Aeronautics(NACA)0015 airfoil during pitching oscillation. The entire construction process is as follows: 1/ Establish a machine learning model based on physical constraints, with training data obtained from Reynolds-Averaged Navier-Stokes(RANS) numerical simulation; 2/ Obtain oscillating airfoil flow field data under experimental conditions through wind tunnel experiments; 3/ On the basis of the above machine learning model, add an experimental data assimilation constraint term to further optimize the training model. Through comparison, we found that the model constructed using data assimilation technology has higher accuracy and can accurately simulate the oscillating airfoil flow field. This data assimilation model has a wide range of applications.

title: Integrated aerostructural design of composite aircraft using inertia relief and multi-objective optimization
abstract: Reducing structural weight and improving performance efficiency are main objectives in next-generation aircraft. Following that, this study has been conducted with the objective of designing a composite aircraft using novel integrated aerostructural design framework that combines inertia-relief-based load estimation, fully coupled static aeroelastic analysis, and surrogate-assisted multi-objective Bayesian optimization (MBO). This study has been conducted in three major steps: (1) inertia relief analysis for load factor estimation, (2) structural sizing of composite aircraft through a fully stressed design (FSD) approach, and (3) MBO incorporating composite materials; carbon fiber–reinforced polymers (CFRPs) and carbon fiber-reinforced thermoplastics (CFRTPs) combinations which offer substantial performance advantages. In this study, Boeing 737-class configuration is used as the reference model. In inertia relief analysis, aerodynamic loads from inviscid Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) were coupled with linear static structural analysis to evaluate load factors estimation which are subsequently incorporated into structural sizing through linear static structural analysis coupled with an iterative fully stressed design (FSD). Finally, MBO enabled aeroelastic consistency across generations, producing Pareto-optimal trade-offs between structural weight and aerodynamic drag. The optimized designs achieved a 20–25% reduction in structural weight while satisfying strength, stiffness, and stability requirements, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed framework for lightweight composite aircraft development.

title: Application of optically enhanced technique-assisted cascaded neural networks to hydrogen extreme combustion flow field reconstruction
abstract: Accurate sensing and prediction of combustion flow dynamics are critical factors for ensuring the reliable operation of scramjet engines under complex operating conditions. Traditional deep learning techniques often neglect the critical optical atomization effects in supersonic combustion flow field reconstruction, resulting in poor visual quality of the reconstructed flow fields. This paper conducts a ground experimental study of a scramjet engine with hydrogen injection pressures of 2 MPa, 3 MPa, and 4 MPa under Ma=3.0 conditions. We propose an Optically Enhanced Cascaded Neural Network (OECNN) assisted by optical enhancement techniques. The method first employs an Encoder-Decoder network for preliminary high-dimensional feature abstraction and compression, followed by the LiteDehazeNet to integrate the extracted features and enhance optical clarity, ultimately generating predicted schlieren images. Finally, a comparative analysis is conducted with the commonly used models Chens, Kongs, and UNet. Experimental results demonstrate that the OECNN model achieves maximum improvements of 56.48% in Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR), 28.33% in Structural Similarity Index Measure (SSIM), and 2.77% in correlation coefficient (R) compared to the other three models. The OECNN achieves an optimal balance between model complexity and accuracy. Compared with existing models, it reduces parameter count by up to 93.54% (merely 41.6 MB), demonstrating the effectiveness of its lightweight design and flow field reconstruction capability.

title: Deep-learning of satellite aerodynamics in very low Earth orbit with partial-physics pretraining
abstract: In very low Earth orbits (VLEOs), orbital decay induced by atmospheric drag is non-trivial, hence accurate aerodynamic models are required for reliable satellite design and mission planning. However, obtaining high-fidelity representations through whole-physics stochastic particle solvers, e.g., Direct Simulation Monte Carlo, for orbit propagation is generally out of reach for most modern computing systems. As such, a deep-learning framework is proposed for cost-effective surrogate modelling of satellite aerodynamics. Models are first pretrained in a cheap partial-physics environment to learn a theory-based component that serves as a baseline, i.e., Sentman’s closed-form solutions for theoretical flat panels. A correction term is then transfer-learned from sparse samples of the whole-physics, high-fidelity aerodynamics to restore the influence from the omitted physics. The models are deployed in several case studies including (i) validation against the GOCE satellite over a selected time window; (ii) orbit propagation of a conceptual satellite; (iii) design study on variation of surface properties. With transfer-learning, models are found to demonstrate improved generalizability and better interpretability according to gradient-based attribution metrics. Using only 14 whole-physics samples for transfer-learning, ground track errors in estimated trajectories obtained through orbit propagation over 20 days, were reduced by 85% as compared to using the partial-physics solver. Considering both offline and online compute costs, transfer-learning incurs up to only 0.87% of the total cost when using whole-physics solvers. By exploiting existing knowledge of partial-physics environments, a scalable and cost-efficient deep-learning framework is discovered for satellite aerodynamics in VLEO.

title: A two-stage physics-informed graph neural network approach for rapid and accurate turbine blade temperature field prediction and data fusion
abstract: Accurate and rapid prediction of the temperature field on turbine blades is critical for the safety, performance, and lifespan of modern gas turbines. Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) and machine learning are two mainstream prediction methods. While CFD provides detailed thermal analysis, it suffers from high computational costs and inherent discrepancies with physical reality. Furthermore, traditional machine learning approaches are not suitable for unstructured meshes and lack physical interpretability. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a two-stage Physics-Informed Graph Neural Network (PIGNN) framework for precise turbine blade temperature prediction and data fusion. In the first stage, a physics embedded GNN model is developed to learn the complex mapping from boundary conditions to the steady-state temperature field across the blade’s unstructured mesh, which explicitly embeds the steady-state heat conduction mechanism into the message passing process of the graph neural network. In the second stage, the framework learns the deviation field between the previous PIGNN’s prediction and sparse, high-fidelity temperature measurements from experiments, effectively fusing the global information from CFD with the local accuracy of experimental data. Results demonstrate that the proposed two-stage PIGNN framework enables fast and accurate temperature field prediction, achieving prediction within 8 ms and the average relative error below 0.41%. Furthermore, when corrected by sparse experimental data, the model’s final prediction error is reduced by 83%. This work presents both a novel PIGNN method for rapid thermal prediction and a robust paradigm for fusing multi-source data to develop reliable digital twins.

title: Multidisciplinary design optimization of distributed electric propulsion aircraft with trim and flying qualities constraints using surrogate models
abstract: Hybrid-electric regional aircraft characterized by distributed electric propulsion offer promising benefits but introduce strong couplings problems between aerodynamics, structures, propulsion, and power systems, requiring a multidisciplinary design and optimization (MDO) approach to capture relevant trade-offs. This work presents an extended MDO framework applied to the Clean Aviation HERA configuration, developed within a collaboration between Politecnico di Milano and Airbus Defence and Space. The framework enhances traditional aero-structural optimization considering the use of the aerodynamic solver DUST, based on Vortex Particle Method (VPM) and by explicitly incorporating stability, control, and automatic trim requirements as design constraints. To limit the computational cost of aerodynamic simulations, surrogate models based on supervised machine learning regression and design of experiments (DOE) are employed within a multi-fidelity strategy. Results show consistent performance improvements in trimmed flight conditions, with successful enforcement of stability and flying qualities constraints. Furthermore, comparison between surrogate-based and high-fidelity optimizations highlights both the accuracy of the reduced-order models and their effectiveness in lowering computational costs.

title: Fusing CFD and measurement data using transfer learning
abstract: Aerodynamic analysis during aircraft design usually involves methods of varying accuracy and spatial resolution, which all have their advantages and disadvantages. It is therefore desirable to create data-driven models which effectively combine these advantages. Such data fusion methods for distributed quantities mainly rely on proper orthogonal decomposition as of now, which is a linear method. In this paper, we introduce a non-linear method based on neural networks combining simulation and measurement data via transfer learning. The network training accounts for the heterogeneity of the data, as simulation data usually features a high spatial resolution, while measurement data is sparse but more accurate. In a first step, the neural network is trained on simulation data to learn spatial features of the distributed quantities. The second step involves transfer learning on the measurement data to correct for systematic errors between simulation and measurement by re-training a subset of the entire neural network model. This approach is applied to a multilayer perceptron architecture and shows significant improvements over the established method based on proper orthogonal decomposition by producing more physical solutions near nonlinearities. In addition, the neural network provides solutions at arbitrary flow conditions, thus making the model useful for flight mechanical design, structural sizing, and certification. As the proposed training strategy is very general, it can also be applied to more complex neural network architectures in the future.

title: A POD-DeepONet based parameter identification framework for the phenomenological model of liquid rocket engine combustion instability
abstract: The stability margin is a key indicator of the operational reliability of liquid rocket engines (LREs). Conventional assessment approaches, such as parameter perturbation and external excitation, often require lengthy testing cycles, incur high costs, and provide limited mechanistic insight, thereby limiting efficient quantitative evaluation of stability characteristics under design-relevant conditions. Recent parameter identification methods based on phenomenological models offer a promising alternative by inferring stability parameters directly from pressure oscillation data. However, these models are formulated as stochastic differential equations, and their identification typically requires solving the inverse problem of the adjoint Fokker–Planck equation (AFP), which involves computationally intensive numerical iterations. To address this challenge, this study develops a POD-DeepONet-based surrogate approach that integrates Proper Orthogonal Decomposition with Deep Operator Networks. By using POD bases extracted from the AFP solution space as a fixed output representation, the framework learns the mapping from phenomenological parameters to finite-time Kramers–Moyal coefficient fields. Results show that POD-DeepONet improves offline training efficiency by 5.2 times and achieves a 2600-fold acceleration in online identification in the tested cases, while maintaining accuracy comparable to the finite-difference method. These results demonstrate its potential for computationally efficient stability-related parameter identification in LRE-oriented phenomenological modeling.

title: Physics-informed digital twin for spacecraft structures under sensor faults: Virtual sensing via a frequency attention U-Net and closed-loop model updating
abstract: Verification and validation (V&V) of structural digital twins becomes fragile when high-frequency Sim-to-Real mismatch coexists with sensor-fault-induced under-observability, as missing channels undermine reliable diagnosis and model updating. To improve trustworthy V&V under partial observation, we present a physics-informed virtual sensing and closed-loop updating framework that reconstructs masked frequency responses and enables stable constrained FEM-parameter updating. Specifically, we couple a reduced-order FEM (ROM) prior with a Frequency Attention U-Net (FAU) that injects Fourier Neural Operator (FNO) global spectral increments through Transformer-gated fusion, driving constrained parameter updating. Systematic experiments on a scaled reconfigurable spacecraft across multiple geometric configurations and two excitation conditions, 10 Hz and 800 Hz, validate the framework’s efficacy. Under 800 Hz excitation, the proposed virtual sensing reduces the log-amplitude main-peak error metric by an average of 76.7 dB under the adopted full-spectrum peak-search protocol. Furthermore, in missing-channel scenarios, the closed-loop updating strategy robustly limits log-amplitude errors on masked channels to 8–10 dB, outperforming spatial interpolation baselines (up to 48 dB error). These improvements reconstruct reliable full-field spectra, supporting physics-consistent interpretation of configuration-dependent joint softening through effective ROM-level parameter trends and providing a foundation for proactive diagnosis and smart maintenance.

title: Large Eddy simulation and data-driven surrogate modeling of high-pressure cryogenic oxygen jets in crossflow
abstract: In this work, the mixing characteristics of a transcritical liquid oxygen jet injected into a vitiated crossflow are investigated at an operating pressure of 100 bar. A comprehensive parametric analysis is performed using Large Eddy Simulations (LES) coupled with tabulated chemistry to decouple the effects of the momentum flux ratio (J) and the jet Reynolds number (Rej). Results indicate that while J primarily governs global jet penetration, Rej significantly affects the near-field topology. At low Reynolds numbers, thermal expansion effects dominate over inertia, leading to a pronounced radial spreading of the dense core, whereas higher Reynolds numbers extend the liquid-like core length. To enable rapid design space exploration, the high-fidelity database is leveraged to train a resolution-invariant surrogate model based on Fourier Neural Operators (FNO). The proposed model accurately infers the time-averaged scalar field and jet trajectory for unseen operating conditions, capturing the non-linearities more effectively than classical empirical correlations. The surrogate demonstrates a speed-up of several orders of magnitude compared to the CFD solver, proving to be a robust tool for the preliminary design of high-pressure propulsion systems.

title: High-fidelity aerodynamic prediction via a physics-informed transformer framework
abstract: Accurate prediction of aerodynamic coefficients for systems with strongly coupled and nonlinear dynamics, such as microspoiler-controlled vehicles, remains challenging in aerospace engineering. Purely data-driven models often lack physical consistency, while classical Physics-Informed Neural Networks are difficult to apply directly to complex three-dimensional aerodynamic flows. This paper proposes the Aero Physics-Informed Network, a data-assisted physics-guided surrogate framework for aerodynamic coefficient prediction. The framework first constructs physically meaningful aerodynamic descriptors from raw operating parameters through physics-guided feature engineering, thereby improving the physical relevance of the input representation without direct PDE-residual optimization. These features are then processed by an Ensemble Kalman Filter-based Physics-Informed Attention mechanism, which refines feature weighting through physically guided updates during learning. The proposed model is trained on high-fidelity CFD data benchmarked against wind tunnel measurements. Comparative, ablation, and robustness studies show that APINN achieves improved predictive accuracy and maintains stronger performance than conventional deep learning baselines under noisy, sparse, and perturbed data conditions. These results indicate that embedding aerodynamic prior knowledge into both feature construction and attention refinement provides an effective and robust surrogate modeling strategy for complex aerodynamic prediction tasks.

title: Fourier feature embedded domain-decomposition physics-informed neural network impedance inversion approach for combustion chamber acoustic boundaries considering mean flow effects
abstract: Acoustic simulations of combustion chambers often exhibit uncertainty due to insufficient understanding of impedance boundary conditions. Recently, the physics-informed neural network (PINN)-based impedance inversion method has been proposed, replacing forward models with data-driven frameworks and breaking the iterative input parameter adjustment cycle of traditional optimization inversion approaches for matching simulated and observational data. However, applying this method to complex combustion chamber acoustic problems presents multiple challenges: complex geometries, heterogeneous acoustic fields, and difficulties in acquiring global training data. In particular, when the influence of mean flow inside the combustion chamber is taken into account, the complexity of the acoustic field increases significantly. Furthermore, direct measurement of velocity perturbations under practical operating conditions is infeasible, which further exacerbates the difficulty in solving impedance inversion problems. Additionally, a single network architecture with unified hyperparameters set struggles to simultaneously capture low and high frequency acoustic field characteristics, preventing stable frequency-independent solutions. To address this, this paper proposes a cross-frequency impedance inversion method based on domain decomposition physics-informed neural networks and Fourier feature embedding, tailored for complex combustion chamber acoustic boundary inversion problems considering the mean flow effect. Case studies conducted impedance inversion on combustion chamber inlet/outlet boundaries considering mean flow effect within the 20–3000 Hz range, where combustion noise is concentrated. Results show the method effectively captures acoustic characteristics even for complex models considering mean flow effect and unknown velocity perturbations, achieving precise inversion of unknown boundary impedances across 20–3000 Hz and providing a viable solution for related engineering problems.

title: Physics-informed neural predictive formation control: A unified framework for safe multi-vehicle coordination
abstract: Multi-vehicle formation control in obstacle-rich environments requires simultaneous optimization of competing objectives including formation maintenance, collision avoidance, and energy efficiency. Existing approaches face two critical limitations: 1) high sensitivity to trade-off parameters, requiring scenario-specific manual tuning when balancing formation maintenance against collision avoidance, and 2) the inherent difficulty of simultaneously optimizing competing objectives, specifically the balance between maintaining formation cohesion and ensuring collision avoidance, which often destabilizes learning and degrades performance. This paper presents Physics-Informed Neural Predictive Formation Control (PINPFC), a unified framework integrating physics-informed neural networks, reinforcement learning, and model predictive control to address these challenges. The PINPFC architecture employs a multi-branch neural network embedding vehicle dynamics, safety constraints, and formation requirements as differentiable physics-informed loss functions, significantly mitigating the need for manual hyperparameter tuning by making competing objectives intrinsic to the network structure. A self-attention mechanism adaptively allocates control authority among branches by learning from real-time formation errors, safety violations, and physical consistency, while the MPC layer ensures hard constraint satisfaction and recursive feasibility. Theoretical analysis establishes formation convergence with explicit ultimate bounds, strict collision avoidance through hierarchical MPC-enforced constraints, and bounded suboptimality relative to centralized control. Comprehensive experimental validation across varying obstacle densities demonstrates that PINPFC achieves measurable improvements in strict success rates and near-collision rates compared to baseline methods, with performance advantages becoming increasingly pronounced in high-density scenarios.

title: A cross-configuration multi-fidelity framework for aerodynamic modeling: DeepONet with adaptive gated fusion and transfer learning
abstract: Accurate prediction of aerodynamic coefficients is essential for guiding aircraft design optimization and performance evaluation. However, existing multi-fidelity surrogate models are typically constrained to narrow geometric training distributions and rely on simplified fusion strategies that lack adaptive weighting. This inability to intelligently fuse heterogeneous fidelity data and extract universal shape-performance relationships causes dramatic performance degradation when evaluating novel configurations, severely limiting their applicability in diverse cross-configuration design scenarios. To address these challenges, we propose a cross-configuration multi-fidelity aerodynamic prediction framework termed DeepONet-GF-TL (Deep Operator Network with Adaptive Gated Fusion and Transfer Learning). The method employs the DeepONet operator architecture as its backbone to decouple geometric and flow-condition feature extraction; integrates an adaptive gated fusion module that dynamically evaluates local data reliability to optimally weight heterogeneous fidelity information across varying flow regimes; introduces a residual skip connection that directly routes raw inputs to the prediction layer, explicitly learning targeted corrections for complex physical mechanisms inherently absent in low-fidelity data; and incorporates a dual-pathway attention mechanism for refined feature representation. On this basis, a two-stage transfer learning strategy with a full-freeze mechanism enables robust cross-configuration generalization on scarce high-fidelity samples while preventing catastrophic forgetting of universal shape-performance mappings. Comprehensive evaluations on 11 subsonic-to-transonic airfoils demonstrate that the proposed DeepONet-GF-TL achieves lift and drag coefficient prediction R2 exceeding 0.995, reducing MAE by 1.7 to 4.6 times compared to three established multi-fidelity baselines(MFGPR, MFNN, and TLNN). Tests on the CACM three-dimensional civil transport aircraft model with 20-dimensional geometric variations confirm robust cross-configuration generalization by accurately predicting the highly nonlinear support interference increments. The proposed method achieves an interference R2 exceeding 0.953 for lift and 0.949 for drag across 450 unseen configurations. Moreover, the method achieves 3 to 4 orders of magnitude speedup over Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD). These results demonstrate that the proposed framework enables accurate and efficient aerodynamic coefficient prediction across diverse geometries, fidelity gap types, and flow conditions.

title: Quantum annealing–based black-box optimization for aerodynamic shape design
abstract: This study proposes a topology optimization framework for aerodynamic shape design based on FMQA (factorization machine with quantum annealing). To address the limited capability of existing topology optimization in exploring global optima, this study aims to enhance global search performance by incorporating quantum annealing. In FMQA, machine learning is used to construct a combinatorial optimization model that is solved by quantum annealing. The proposed method is applied to the optimization of a single-element airfoil, and both QUBO (quadratic unconstrained binary optimization) and Ising formulations are investigated. The results show that the Ising model outperforms the QUBO model due to its higher learnability in machine learning. The effect of regularization is also examined, demonstrating that it suppresses overfitting and leads to smoother, physically meaningful geometries. The optimal geometry includes a Gurney flap-like structure at the trailing edge, which significantly improves aerodynamic performance. The results highlight the potential of the proposed FMQA-based topology optimization framework for discovering high-performance and non-intuitive aerodynamic designs.

title: Geometry-aware, CAD-free, and differentiable closed-form surrogates for lifting surface mass estimation via symbolic regression with autonomous similarity scaling
abstract: Accurate structural mass estimation of lifting surfaces is required throughout aircraft design, yet existing methods cannot simultaneously provide closed-form geometric descriptors, physically consistent similarity scaling, and exact differentiability without repeated three-dimensional geometry instantiation. This work presents a symbolic-regression (SR) framework for segment-level mass estimation of solid, skin-laminated, shell, and wing-box lifting surfaces, using external surface area and enclosed volume as governing mass descriptors and quasi-analytical rib and spar volume expressions for internal contributions. A parameterized wing-segment dataset was generated in OpenVSP over the 2–25 kg MTOW range, consistent with harmonized UAV regulatory frameworks, using planform variables and Class–Shape Transformation airfoil coefficients to cover the admissible geometric envelope. From this database, closed-form SR models and a Bayesian-optimized deep neural network (DNN) benchmark were trained on identical data partitions, with compact reduced models subsequently derived via partial-elasticity analysis. The SR models provide CAD-free, closed-form, and exactly differentiable surrogate equations, with dimensional-homogeneity filtering on the Pareto front enforcing physically consistent similarity scaling, recovering dimensional laws autonomously—without repeated geometry instantiation. Full SR surrogates achieved R 2 ≥ 0.9997, while elasticity-guided reduced models preserved R 2 ≥ 0.9994. In external validation over CAD-reconstructed aircraft spanning 1.9–3, 629 kg, SR yielded mean segment-level errors of 1.80 % for surface area and 0.96 % for enclosed volume, outperforming the DNN (1.84 % and 1.61 %) while reducing evaluation time by up to 63 × . Reduced models achieved mean errors below 1.40 %, and quasi-analytical internal estimates remained below 3.64 %. Experimental validation on the fabricated Fénix UAV wing confirmed a total mass error of 2.74 %, with component-level errors below 3.80 %.

title: Learning aerodynamic optimization of three-dimensional high-lift configurations based on reinforcement learning in two-dimensional flow field environment
abstract: Reinforcement Learning (RL) has demonstrated significant potential for learning and leveraging experience in aerodynamic design optimization. Through extensive agent-environment interactions, generalizable optimization policies can be acquired. However, applying RL to three-dimensional (3D) aerodynamic optimization remains challenging due to the high computational cost of Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) during training. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a novel RL-based 2D-to-3D framework that trains an optimization policy in a low-cost 2D CFD environment and directly deploys it to 3D high-lift configurations. The policy is trained using the Double Deep Q-Network algorithm, requiring only 483 samples of 2D aerodynamic data. Velocity field features are extracted through Two-Directional Two-Dimensional Principal Component Analysis to provide physical information for the agent’s decision-making. This physics-informed policy learning strategy underlies the generalizability of the learned policy across various flow conditions and its direct application to 3D configurations without further learning. While the optimal design parameters can differ substantially between 2D and 3D configurations, the velocity field features linked to aerodynamic performance, which have been learned by the agent in 2D environment, show remarkable similarity when both configurations attain their optimal states. Results show that the proposed framework efficiently trains an optimization policy applicable to various 3D high-lift configurations at minimal computational cost. The policy exhibits high efficiency and strong generalizability in optimizing both 2D and 3D high-lift configurations under varying flow conditions, flap deflections, and wing planforms.

title: A method for reconstructing the line-of-sight pointing of remote sensing satellites using a multimodal neural network integrated with FBG sensor networks
abstract: On-orbit monitoring of line-of-sight (LOS) pointing deviation is crucial for improving the target positioning accuracy of geostationary orbit (GEO) satellites. However, it remains a challenging task. To address this problem, this paper proposes a LOS pointing monitoring method based on an Fiber Bragg Grating(FBG) sensor network and a multimodal neural network. By deploying the FBG sensor network on the remote sensing payload support structure, high-precision measurement of the temperature and strain fields is achieved. A CNN-Transformer cascade neural network is then used to predict variations in LOS pointing. Specifically, the Convolutional Neural Network(CNN) extracts high-dimensional features from the FBG spectrum at each sensor location, and the Transformer performs multimodal fusion of these spectral features with the structural strain and temperature fields data, thereby improving the accuracy of the LOS pointing deviation prediction. This study specifically targets quasi-static thermal deformations of GEO satellites, where the thermal environment changes slowly and dynamic effects are negligible. A simplified model of the support structure for remote sensing payloads was constructed, and simulation experiments were carried out. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method can effectively monitor LOS pointing deviations caused by micro-deformation of the payload support structure, achieving a prediction accuracy that exceeds 98.3 %. This study provides a promising approach for high-precision on-orbit monitoring quasi-static, thermally induced LOS pointing deviations in GEO satellites.
